title: Explainable machine learning model based on cardiac CT angiography for predicting functional improvement after atrial fibrillation ablation: a multicenter study
summary: Radiofrequency ablation is an established therapy for atrial fibrillation (AF), but outcomes are heterogeneous in patients with concomitant heart failure (HF). Therefore, we aimed to develop an explainable machine learning (ML) model based on cardiac CT angiography (CTA) for predicting functional improvement after ablation in patients with AF combined with HF. Patients at our institution were randomly divided into training and validation sets in the ratio of 7:3 and two other organizations were included as testing sets. Morphological features of the left atrium (LA) and pulmonary vein (PV) and radiomics features of the left atrial wall (LAW) were extracted, and Shape and Wall models were constructed using the ML algorithm, respectively. Shape_score and Wall_ score were calculated and integrated with important clinical factors to construct a combined predictive model (COMB). The predictive performance of the model was assessed by area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). Shapley additive explanations (SHAP) were used to interpret the contributions of individual features. 240, 101, and 75 patients were included in the training, validation, and testing sets, respectively. Gender, hyperlipidemia, urea, and AF type were retained in the final clinical model. Two shapes and three LAW radiomics features were screened to build Shape and Wall models, respectively. The developed COMB model presented good performance in predicting functional improvement after ablation in the three sets (AUC = 0.866, 0.803, and 0.845). SHAP analysis revealed the features with the greatest impact on the prediction outcomes in the Shape and Wall models. The model integrating cardiac CTA-derived morphological and radiomics features with clinical factors showed potential for predicting functional improvement after ablation in patients with AF and HF. Further prospective evaluation is required before clinical implementation.

title: Point-of-care ultrasound for left ventricular function in patients with atrial fibrillation in the emergency department.
summary:
INTRODUCTION: There is a knowledge gap regarding reliability of point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) assessing left ventricular function for patients in acute rapid atrial fibrillation (AF) or flutter (AFL) in the emergency department (ED). We sought to evaluate interrater agreement of POCUS severely reduced left ventricular function in this ED population.

METHODS: We conducted a health records review of adult patients who presented with rapid AF/AFL, heart rate above 110, to a tertiary care hospital ED. POCUS scans archived by ED physicians were interpreted by two cardiologists and one ED POCUS expert. Left ventricular function was categorized as either 'normal or non-severely reduced' and 'severely reduced' function. Interrater agreement analysis was performed using Cohen's kappa with 95% confidence interval (CI).

RESULTS: We identified 332 ED patients with acute rapid AF/AFL during our study period, of which 128(38%) had POCUS assessing left ventricular function. All archived POCUS scans (100/128) were used for agreement analysis. We found a moderate level of agreement between cardiologists and ED POCUS expert (k = 0.63 CI 95% 0.43-0.82) with an 88% raw agreement (74% normal or non-severe, 14% severely reduced). Fair agreement was found between cardiologists and ED physicians (k = 0.34 CI 95% 0.10-0.58) 85% raw agreement (80% normal or non-severe, 5% severely reduced).

CONCLUSION: Among patients with rapid AF/AFL evaluated in the ED, one-third had POCUS left ventricular function assessments. ED physicians and ED POCUS expert agreement with cardiologists ranged from fair to moderate when distinguishing severely reduced left ventricular function from normal or non-severely reduced function in patients with rapid AF/AFL. These findings are a first step in demonstrating the reliability of POCUS left ventricular function assessment in patients presenting with rapid AF/AFL to the ED.

title: Substrate-Dependent Pro- and Antiarrhythmic Action of Omecamtiv Mecarbil at the Ventricular and Atrial Level: Insights from a Langendorff-Perfused Rabbit Heart Model
summary: Omecamtiv mecarbil is a cardiac-selective myosin activator and potential heart failure treatment, but its electrophysiological profile remains incompletely characterized. We investigated omecamtiv mecarbil in a Langendorff-perfused rabbit heart model. Forty-eight rabbit hearts were retrogradely perfused; twenty-four in a ventricular and twenty-four in an atrial setup. In the ventricular setup, action potential duration at 90% repolarization (APD90), QT interval, and dispersion of repolarization were assessed during pacing at seven cycle lengths. After baseline recordings, Group 1 (n = 12) received 1, 5 and 10 µM omecamtiv mecarbil sequentially, while Group 2 (n = 12) received 100 µM sotalol followed by 5 µM omecamtiv mecarbil. In the atrial setup, Group 3 (n = 12) received 5 and 10 µM omecamtiv mecarbil, and Group 4 (n = 12) received isoproterenol/acetylcholine (IsoACh) to increase atrial fibrillation (AF) susceptibility, followed by 5 µM omecamtiv mecarbil. Omecamtiv mecarbil alone shortened ventricular APD90 and QT interval, increased dispersion of repolarization, and raised ventricular arrhythmia incidence. Sotalol prolonged APD90, QT interval, and dispersion, with a marked rise in VT episodes; additional omecamtiv mecarbil did not further prolong repolarization but increased arrhythmia susceptibility further. In the atrial setup, omecamtiv mecarbil alone prolonged conduction time and increased AF inducibility. Under IsoACh, which shortened atrial APD and refractoriness and increased AF episodes, additional omecamtiv mecarbil slowed atrial conduction and markedly suppressed AF. In summary, omecamtiv mecarbil was proarrhythmic at the ventricular level, particularly under reduced repolarization reserve, but showed antiarrhythmic effects in an IsoACh-induced AF model and proarrhythmic properties in the healthy atrium, indicating a substrate-dependent electrophysiological profile.

title: Atrial Fibrillation in Tribal and Non-tribal Populations: A Comparative Analysis From Eastern India
summary: BackgroundAtrial fibrillation (AF) is an increasingly prevalent arrhythmia in India, where rheumatic heart disease and cardiometabolic etiologies coexist.This study compared the demographic profile, clinical presentation, associated clinical conditions, echocardiographic characteristics, thromboembolic risk, and anticoagulation practices between tribal patients and non-tribal patients in Eastern India. MethodsThis retrospective hospital-based cross-sectional study included 364 consecutive adult patients with AF (106 tribal and 258 non-tribal patients) admitted between January 2022 and December 2024.Clinical, electrocardiographic, echocardiographic, and treatment data were extracted from hospital records.Continuous variables were compared using Welch's t-test and categorical variables using Pearson's chisquare test. ResultsTribal patients more frequently presented with first-diagnosed AF (81/106, 76.4% vs. 153/258, 59.3%; p = 0.002), higher ventricular rates (112.6 ± 25.1 vs. 102.3± 19.6 beats/min; p < 0.001), lower left ventricular ejection fraction (46.0 ± 11.7% vs. 51.0 ± 10.5%; p < 0.001), and more heart failure symptoms at presentation (27/106, 25.4% vs. 41/258, 15.9%; p = 0.033).Lifestyle-related risk factors were significantly more prevalent among tribal patients (79/106, 74.5% vs. 137/258, 53.1%; p < 0.001).Conversely, non-tribal patients had a higher prevalence of cardiometabolic disorders (168/258, 65.1% vs. 43/106, 40.6%; p < 0.001), ischemic cardiovascular disease (69/258, 26.7% vs. 18/106, 17.0%; p = 0.047), chronic kidney disease (93/258, 36.0%vs. 25/106, 23.6%; p = 0.021), higher CHA₂DS₂-VASc scores (2.38 ± 1.66 vs. 1.86 ± 1.45; p = 0.004), and a greater proportion meeting criteria for long-term oral anticoagulation (192/258, 74.4% vs. 67/106, 63.2%; p = 0.032).Rheumatic heart disease, heart failure, left atrial thrombus, ischemic stroke, and anticoagulant prescribing patterns were comparable between the two groups. ConclusionsTribal patients with AF had more first-diagnosed AF, higher ventricular rates, lower left ventricular systolic function, and greater lifestyle-related risk factors, whereas non-tribal patients had greater cardiometabolic and thromboembolic risk.These findings demonstrate differences in the clinical presentation and risk profile of AF within this hospital-based cohort and highlight the need for population-specific strategies to improve AF detection, prevention, and management in Eastern India.

title: Non-alcoholic Fatty Liver Disease/Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease and the Risk of Incident Atrial Fibrillation: An Updated Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Cohort Studies
summary: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), formerly non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD), has been inconsistently linked to incident atrial fibrillation (AF) across observational cohorts.We performed an updated systematic review and meta-analysis of cohort studies, following the Meta-analysis Of Observational Studies in Epidemiology (MOOSE) guidelines, searching PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, and Web of Science through July 25, 2026, for studies comparing incident AF risk in adults with versus without NAFLD/MASLD.Adjusted effect estimates were pooled using a random-effects model, with heterogeneity assessed via the I² statistic and explored through subgroup and univariable meta-regression analyses.Eighteen cohort studies comprising over 15 million participants from Asia, Europe, and North America met inclusion criteria.Pooling all studies demonstrated a significantly increased risk of incident AF among individuals with NAFLD/MASLD compared with those without (pooled risk ratio (RR) 1.23, 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.12-1.34,p < 0.001), with substantial statistical heterogeneity (I² = 99.4%).In an exploratory analysis of three studies, advanced disease with hepatic fibrosis was also associated with increased AF risk (RR 1.19, 95% CI 1.11-1.28).In the present meta-analysis, NAFLD/MASLD was associated with a modestly higher risk of incident AF after adjustment for conventional cardiometabolic risk factors, although heterogeneity was very high.These findings support attention to AF risk in this population and the use of standardized diagnostic approaches in future research.

title: Echocardiographic Framework for Left Atrial Appendage Morphology Assessment and Thromboembolic Risk Stratification in Atrial Fibrillation
summary: Background: Left Atrial Appendage (LAA) causes a thrombus risk in patients with atrial fibrillation (AF). Accurate identification of LAA morphology reduces thrombotic stroke. Methods: This study proposes a hybrid deep learning framework, Left Atrial Appendage Thrombus Framework (LAATF), which integrates Adaptive CLAHE, optimized Chan-Vese contour extraction, and a multi-headed AgileFormer transformer to classify LAA morphology, detect thrombus, and estimate image-derived thromboembolic risk using the LightGBM-based proposed Thromboembolic Risk index (TRI) score. A dataset of 4320 temporal images from 240 patients with AF was used, comprising four LAA morphologies (chicken-wing, windsock, cactus, and cauliflower). CLAHE enhanced local contrast. The Chan-Vese model delineated appendage contours. AgileFormer extracted image-derived textural and morphological features to classify morphology and thrombus presence. LightGBM-based TRI regression estimated thromboembolic risk in AF patients with LAA. Results: The proposed framework achieved a morphology classification accuracy of 91-94% and thrombus detection AUC of 0.935, with a sensitivity of 93.4% and specificity of 92.6%. The computed TRI correlated strongly with actual outcomes (R2 = 0.98, r = 0.99). Among morphologies, cauliflower and cactus types show the highest thromboembolic risk due to their increased texture entropy and image-based features. Conclusions: The LAATF framework provides an interpretable, image-based technique for LAA morphology assessment and thrombus prediction.

title: Exploratory Signal Detection of Arrhythmia Reports for Empagliflozin, Sitagliptin, and Linagliptin in the Korea Adverse Event Reporting System
summary: Studies have reported cardiovascular effects of Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) and dipeptidyl peptidase-4 (DPP-4) inhibitors.Although cardiovascular and renal benefits of SGLT2 inhibitors have been reported, their specific association with arrhythmias such as atrial fibrillation (AF), atrial flutter, and ventricular fibrillation remains less clearly defined.Therefore, this study aims to investigate the association between empagliflozin, sitagliptin, and linagliptin and reporting patterns of selected arrhythmias in Koreans.Raw data from the Korea Adverse Event Reporting System database were analyzed from January 2019 to December 2023.The drugs of interest were SGLT2 and DPP-4 inhibitors; however, the final disproportionality analysis was limited to empagliflozin, sitagliptin, and linagliptin because these were the drugs with relevant analyzable arrhythmia reports in the study dataset.The analyzed adverse events included atrial fibrillation (AF), atrial flutter, and ventricular fibrillation.The association between the drugs and adverse events was evaluated using disproportionality analysis and chi-squared testing in SAS software version 9.7.Disproportionality analyses revealed that empagliflozin, sitagliptin, and linagliptin showed no positive reporting signals for AF, atrial flutter, and ventricular fibrillation based on the prespecified signal detection criteria.The chi-squared test showed a statistically significant association between each drug and adverse events (p < 0.001); which was interpreted as a difference in reporting distributions within the spontaneous reporting dataset, not as evidence of clinical risk or causality.The findings indicate that selected arrhythmia terms were not disproportionately reported for empagliflozin, sitagliptin, and linagliptin in the KAERS DB during the study period.However, since this analysis was based on collected unsolicited data and the statistical results are limited to signal detection, further studies using global datasets and large-scale clinical trials are needed.

title: Trends in the incidence of atrial fibrillation and the prescription of oral anticoagulants in adults with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease in UK primary care (2010–2022): a cohort study
summary: Background Understanding the burden of atrial fibrillation (AF) and oral anticoagulant (OAC) use in patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is important for stroke prevention in this high-risk population. We assessed trends in AF incidence and OAC initiation among patients with COPD in UK primary care from 2010 to 2022.Methods We assembled a cohort of all patients at least 50 years of age who contributed data to the UK Clinical Practice Research Datalink between January 1, 2010, and December 31, 2022, who had a physician diagnosis of COPD before or during the study period. Patients were followed-up until AF diagnosis, study end date (December 2022), death, or transfer out of practice. We estimated annual incidence rates of AF and subsequent OAC initiation using Poisson regression, stratified by age, sex, ethnicity, and COPD severity. We assessed predictors of AF and OAC initiation using Cox proportional hazards regression models.Findings 444,668 patients with COPD were included (mean age 70 years, 51.8% male), contributing 2,284,799 person-years of follow-up. 37,645 (8.5%) patients were diagnosed with AF during the study period. The incidence of AF increased from 13.8 per 1000 person-years in 2010 to 19.3 in 2022 [rate ratio (RR) 1.29; 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.07-1.56], and was higher in males, White individuals, those over 80 years, and patients with severe COPD. Only 23,094 patients (66.3%) were prescribed an OAC in the year following AF diagnosis, though OAC use increased 2.9-fold during this period (RR 2.91; 95% CI 2.33-3.65). OAC initiation remained lowest among patients aged 50-59 and ≥90 years, and non-White individuals. OAC use was also up to 25.0% (adjusted hazard ratio 0.75; 95% CI 0.69, 0.81) less prevalent among those with severe COPD.Interpretation AF incidence and OAC initiation increased among patients with COPD in UK primary care over 2010-2022. However, OAC use remained suboptimal, especially among older patients, non-White individuals, and those with severe COPD. These potential treatment gaps highlight the need for further research on stroke prevention strategies in this high-risk population.Funding This research received no specific grant from any funding agency in the public, commercial or not-for-profit sectors.

title: Cardiometabolic therapy for rhythm control: a case report of refractory atrial fibrillation resolving after initiation of semaglutide for obesity
summary: Background Obesity is a major modifiable risk factor for atrial fibrillation (AF) and has been linked to processes involved in atrial structural and electrical remodelling. Glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonists reduce cardiovascular events in patients with type 2 diabetes at high cardiovascular risk and are increasingly regarded as cardiometabolic therapies. Whether these agents modify the trajectory of atrial cardiomyopathy or exert direct antiarrhythmic effects beyond their metabolic actions remains an area of active investigation.Case summary A 50-year-old man with obesity (body mass index 34.9 kg/m2) and persistent AF presented with persistent symptomatic episodes despite four prior pulmonary vein isolation procedures and repeated electrical cardioversions. Rhythm monitoring was performed continuously using a wearable device since 2023, documenting recurrent episodes lasting 8-30 h with a modified European Heart Rhythm Association (mEHRA) class IIb-III symptom burden. Echocardiography demonstrated preserved left ventricular systolic function and left atrial enlargement. In January 2026, once-weekly subcutaneous semaglutide was initiated for weight management (0.25 mg/week with subsequent dose escalation). While a weight reduction of 14 kg was observed within 6 months, AF episodes and symptoms ceased immediately after treatment initiation and have not recurred during follow-up.Conclusion This case describes cessation of recurrent AF episodes following initiation of semaglutide in a patient with obesity and prior ablation failure. Potential mechanisms may include cardiometabolic effects as well as direct myocardial effects on sodium and calcium handling that have been described experimentally. Although a causal relationship cannot be established from a single observation, this finding may serve as a hypothesis-generating signal and provide a rationale for prospective studies evaluating cardiometabolic therapies as potential adjuncts in rhythm control strategies.

title: γ-Butyrobetaine, L-Carnitine and Acylcarnitines and their association with incident atrial fibrillation among men and women with suspected chronic coronary syndrome
summary: Abstract Background Carnitine-metabolites play a key role in cell energy metabolism and has been implicated in the pathogenesis of atrial fibrillation (AF). However, any associations between L-carnitine and the precursor γ-butyrobetaine (γBB) with new-onset AF are not established. We therefore examined the relationship between serum γBB, L-carnitine and selected acylcarnitines with incident AF. Methods We studied 3815 patients who underwent coronary angiography due to suspected chronic coronary syndrome and followed up for incident CVD events, including new-onset AF. Risk associations between the biomarkers and incident AF were explored by logistic regression for the total population and stratified according to sex. Results The majority (71.6 %) of the patients were men, the median age was 61 years. Over a median follow-up of 7.3 years, 412 (10.8 %) were reported with new-onset AF. In a multivariate model higher serum γBB, L-carnitine and palmitoylcarnitine (OR per 1SD [95 % CI] : 1.15 [1.01-1.31], P = 0.04; 1.14 [1.01-1.27], P = 0.03 and 1.15 [1.03-1.28], P = 0.01) were associated with increased risk of incident AF. These associations were particularly stronger among women (P for interaction < 0.04, all). Conclusion In this large cohort of patients with suspected chronic coronary syndrome elevated circulating levels of γBB, L-carnitine and palmitoylcarnitine were associated with increased risk of incident AF, with stronger associations among women. Our results motivate further studies examining the relationship between carnitine metabolites and cardiac arrythmias and highlight the need for sex specific analyses.

title: Supplemental Material for: Population Mortality Involving Co-Reported Intracerebral Hemorrhage and Atrial Fibrillation or Flutter in the United States, 1999–2025: Trends, Demographic Disparities, and Forecasts to 2040
summary: Introduction: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is the most common indication for long-term oral anticoagulation, and intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) is the most feared bleeding complication of that treatment. National mortality data describing deaths in which both conditions are recorded remain limited. Temporal, demographic, and geographic trends in United States population mortality involving co-reported ICH and AF or atrial flutter from 1999 to 2025, with projections to 2040, were examined. Methods: A retrospective analysis of death certificate data from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention Wide-ranging Online Data for Epidemiologic Research (CDC WONDER) database was conducted, identifying deaths listing ICH (International Classification of Diseases, Tenth Revision [ICD-10] code I61) and AF or atrial flutter (ICD-10 code I48) in any cause-of-death field. Records were extracted on June 15, 2026; data for 1999 through 2024 came from final Multiple Cause of Death files and data for 2025 from the provisional file. Age-adjusted mortality rates (AAMRs) were calculated per 100,000 total resident United States population and stratified by sex, race/ethnicity, census region, and urbanization. Joinpoint regression assessed temporal trends, and autoregressive integrated moving average (ARIMA) models projected rates through 2040. Results: From 1999 to 2025, 52,967 deaths with co-reported ICH and AF or atrial flutter were identified. The overall age-adjusted mortality rate rose from 0.4 to 0.7 per 100,000 between 1999 and 2021 (annual percent change [APC] 1.53%, p=0.016) before stabilizing through 2025. AAMRs were higher among men than among women in every study year and increased across the study period among Black or African American decedents (APC 1.83%, p<0.000001). Rates were highest in the West, which recorded the highest regional rate in every study year, and in nonmetropolitan areas, which exceeded metropolitan rates in every year from 2012 onward; the Northeast was the only region with a significant decline after 2015. Pooled state AAMRs ranged from 0.3 in Louisiana to 1.1 in Vermont, and 75.4% of deaths occurred in medical facilities. Conclusions: Population mortality involving co-reported ICH and AF or atrial flutter rose until 2021 and then stabilized, with differences by sex, race and ethnicity, and geography that persisted across the study period. Age-adjusted rates are projected to remain broadly stable through 2040. These findings are descriptive. They do not establish that AF, anticoagulation, or anticoagulation-associated bleeding caused the hemorrhages recorded, and differences in hypertension control and anticoagulation management remain plausible but untested explanations that warrant direct study.

title: Development of an efficient deep learning model for arrhythmia detection from consumer smartwatches
summary: Introduction Cardiac arrhythmias often progress without clear symptoms and may remain undetected until severe complications occur. Continuous monitoring through consumer smartwatches offers a scalable and non-invasive opportunity for real-time rhythm screening in free-living conditions. However, wrist-based photoplethysmography (PPG) signals are highly susceptible to motion artifacts and inter-subject variability, limiting traditional signal-processing techniques. In this work, we compare classical machine learning and deep learning approaches for multi-class arrhythmia classification from real-life smartwatch PPG and accelerometer recordings collected in the Pulsewatch clinical trial. Three rhythm categories are considered: normal sinus rhythm (NSR), atrial fibrillation (AF), and premature atrial or ventricular contractions (PAC/PVC).Methods The evaluated approaches include a Random Forest classifier based on engineered temporal and morphological features, together with two end-to-end architectures, CNN-GRU and CNN-BiLSTM, designed to learn temporal patterns directly from raw two-channel smartwatch waveforms while addressing motion artifacts, sensor noise, and cross-subject generalization.Results Under two-fold subject-independent cross-validation, the Random Forest achieved the highest average accuracy among the proposed methods (91.22%), together with the best macro precision (85.89%), macro F1 score (84.17%), and macro ROC-AUC (97.03%). The CNN-BiLSTM achieved the highest macro recall (87.37%), indicating stronger sensitivity to arrhythmic classes, while the CNN-GRU remained competitive with a macro recall of 86.85% and a macro F1 score of 83.13%.Discussion Compared with the Pulsewatch baselines reported by Han et al., the proposed methods improved the available macro-level metrics, with the Random Forest obtaining the strongest macro precision and macro F1 score and the CNN-BiLSTM the strongest macro recall, indicating improved class-balanced recognition of clinically relevant arrhythmic events. These results show that feature-based models remain highly competitive for smartwatch-based arrhythmia detection, achieving the strongest overall and macro F1 performance among the proposed methods, while hybrid convolutional-recurrent architectures provide increased sensitivity to minority rhythm classes. Deployment-oriented profiling under an identical single-core benchmark showed a mean end-to-end inference time of 33.08 ms for the Random Forest pipeline and 51.87 ms for the CNN-BiLSTM model on a 30-s segment, supporting near-real-time rhythm screening.Conclusion Overall, this work highlights the trade-offs between the analyzed approaches in terms of accuracy, class-balanced performance, computational complexity, and deployment feasibility for wearable cardiac monitoring systems.

title: Attenuating cardiac sympathetic tone via cryoneurolytic stellate ganglion ablation.
summary:
BACKGROUND: Stellate ganglion (SG) blockade provides temporary control of refractory ventricular arrhythmias by reducing sympathetic flow to the heart. However, current percutaneous approaches are limited by their short duration of effect, creating a need for longer-lasting sympathetic modulation without more invasive permanent sympathectomy.

OBJECTIVE: To determine the efficacy and durability of SG cryoneurolytic ablation in attenuating evoked cardiac sympathetic responses.

METHODS: We conducted acute cryoablation studies in 6 Yorkshire pigs and chronic studies in 10 Yucatan minipigs (7 cryoablation and 3 sham controls). Acute studies evaluated hemodynamic responses and myocardial norepinephrine release using fast-scanning cyclic voltammetry. Chronic studies assessed the 1-month physiological, electrophysiological, neurochemical, and histologic effects following right SG cryoneurolytic ablation.

RESULTS: Cryoneurolytic SG ablation attenuated evoked cardiac sympathetic responses in both acute and chronic phases. One month following ablation, sympathetic attenuation persisted and was accompanied by significant treatment effects on ventricular repolarization. Sympathetic attenuation remained anatomically restricted to the ablation site, and targeting the T1 component of the SG alone was sufficient to eliminate the majority of evoked sympathetic cardiac effects.

CONCLUSION: Cryoneurolytic SG ablation effectively provides durable cardiac sympathetic modulation, offering a promising intermediate-duration treatment for refractory ventricular arrhythmias.

title: Direct atrial fibrillation termination during pulsed field ablation: Association with intracardiac cycle length.
summary:
BACKGROUND: Pulsed field ablation (PFA) enables rapid and tissue-selective pulmonary vein isolation (PVI). However, the electrophysiological determinants of direct atrial fibrillation (AF) termination during PFA remain unclear.

OBJECTIVE: To investigate the clinical and electrophysiological characteristics associated with direct AF termination during PFA-guided PVI.

METHODS: This prospective, single-center study included 72 patients with persistent AF undergoing PFA-based PVI. Intracardiac tachycardia cycle length (TCL) was measured at each pulmonary vein before ablation. Patients were classified into termination and no-termination groups, and clinical and electrophysiological parameters were compared.

RESULTS: Direct AF termination occurred in 14 patients (19.4%), most frequently at the right superior pulmonary vein (RSPV) (n = 8), followed by the Left superior pulmonary vein (LSPV) (n = 6). Patients with termination had shorter AF duration, smaller left atrial size, and lower NT-proBNP levels. TCL at the superior pulmonary veins, particularly the RSPV, was significantly longer in the termination group, while no differences were observed at other pulmonary veins. At 3 months, AF recurrence tended to be lower in the termination group, although the difference did not reach statistical significance.

CONCLUSION: Direct AF termination during PFA is associated with favorable clinical characteristics and localized TCL prolongation in the superior pulmonary veins, suggesting their important role in AF maintenance rather than a purely random procedural effect.

title: Transient changes in P-wave terminal force after electrical cardioversion of persistent atrial fibrillation
summary: Background P-wave terminal force in lead V1 (PWTFV1) reflects left atrial remodeling and is associated with atrial fibrillation (AF) outcomes, but its time course after electrical cardioversion of persistent AF is unclear.Methods We retrospectively analyzed 108 patients with persistent AF after successful electrical cardioversion, with 12‑lead electrocardiograms at 30 min, 1 month, and 3 months. Terminal P-wave duration (PNTV1) and amplitude (PNAV1) in lead V1 were measured and PWTFV1 calculated as their product; changes are expressed in absolute magnitude. Correlations with left atrial diameter and categorical classification (abnormal if magnitude ≥4000 ms·μV) were assessed.Results PNTV1 increased at 1 month versus 30 min (60 ± 25 vs 58 ± 19 ms; P = 0.018) and returned to baseline at 3 months (57 ± 19 ms; P = 0.83; Friedman P = 0.031). PNAV1 was unchanged (P = 0.37). PWTFV1 increased transiently in magnitude at 1 month (-4294 ± 2545 vs -4079 ± 2138 ms·μV; P = 0.022) and normalized at 3 months (-4039 ± 2060 ms·μV; P = 0.64). PWTFV1 did not correlate with left atrial diameter (all |ρ| ≈ 0.05, P ≥ 0.61), and categorical classification was unchanged (57/108 abnormal throughout; no patient reclassified).Conclusion PWTFV1 shows transient, duration-driven variability after cardioversion, peaking at 1 month. The change is small, does not alter categorical classification, and is not mirrored by left atrial size, consistent with ongoing atrial recovery rather than stable remodeling. Timing of assessment matters when PWTFV1 is interpreted as a continuous measure.

title: Effects of Dual-Energy Lattice-Tip Catheter Ablation of Ventricular Arrhythmias on Cardiac Implantable Electronic Device Performance
summary: Background The Sphere-9 lattice-tip catheter (Affera, Medtronic) enables delivery of both radiofrequency ablation (RFA) and pulsed field ablation (PFA) for ventricular arrhythmia (VA) ablation. Data on its impact on cardiac implantable electronic devices (CIEDs) are limited.Objectives This study sought to evaluate changes in CIED function following VA ablation using the Sphere-9 catheter.Methods We reviewed 65 consecutive patients (median age 71 years, 94% male, 63% ischemic cardiomyopathy, median left ventricular ejection fraction 31%) with pre-existing CIEDs who underwent VA ablation (62 ventricular tachycardia [95%], 3 premature ventricular contraction [5%]) using the Sphere-9 catheter (combined RFA/PFA (53 [82%]), RFA alone (6 [9%]), PFA alone (6 [9%])). Device interrogation was performed within 30 days preprocedure, within 7 days postprocedure, and at 3-month (+/- 30 days) follow-up.Results At 3-months, right ventricular leads demonstrated reduced sensing amplitude (11.7-10.0 mV, P = 0.04), pacing impedance (441-422 Ω, P < 0.001), shock impedance (64-59 Ω, P = 0.01), and increased capture threshold (0.9-1.0 V at 0.4-0.5 milliseconds, P = 0.03). Left ventricular (LV) leads demonstrated reduced pacing impedance (544-475 Ω, P = 0.04), whereas LV capture threshold remained elevated (1.0-1.4 V, P = 0.08). Right atrial lead parameters remained stable. No patient required CIED revision. One patient experienced cardiac resynchronization therapy-D pulse generator failure during PFA delivery 7.5 mm from an LV lead tip electrode, requiring generator replacement.Conclusions Ventricular arrhythmia ablation using the Sphere-9 dual-energy lattice-tip catheter was associated with small but persistent changes in right and left ventricular lead parameters. Serious CIED interactions were uncommon, and further studies are needed to better understand the underlying mechanisms.

Medication Errors Associated with Direct Oral Anticoagulant Therapy: A Systematic Review
summary: Direct Oral Anticoagulants (DOACs) such as dabigatran, rivaroxaban, apixaban, and edoxaban are now widely used in the treatment and prevention of various blood clotting disorders, including atrial fibrillation and venous thromboembolism. Direct Oral Anticoagulants (DOACs) such as dabigatran, rivaroxaban, apixaban, and edoxaban have become the primary choice for stroke prevention in atrial fibrillation and for the prevention and treatment of venous thromboembolism (VTE). Although DOACs are considered more practical and safer than previous medications like warfarin, medication errors, especially regarding dosage and administration, can still occur while the drug is in use. This error can significantly affect the patient's condition, so it's important to know how often this problem occurs and its causes. This systematic review aims to determine the prevalence of medication errors associated with DOACs in clinical practice and to identify contributing factors related to DOACs in adult patients using the human factors model. This study was conducted using a systematic method based on PRISMA guidelines. Three major databases—PubMed, Scopus, and Google Scholar—were used to search for data, and the study covers the period from 2015 to 2025. The studies analysed were observational studies reporting DOAC misuse in adult patients. Systematic reviews, studies in children or animals, and non-clinical research were not included. From 1,434 screened articles, 11 relevant studies were selected. The most frequent errors occur during prescribing, particularly those related to inappropriate, too low, or non-compliant dosages. Some studies show that over 30% of patients receive inappropriate doses. Inappropriate drug combinations or the selection of an unsuitable DOAC for a patient's specific condition also frequently lead to errors. The types of DOACs most commonly associated with errors are rivaroxaban and apixaban. Medication Errors in the use of DOACs remain a significant problem in the clinical world. Incorrect dosage and improper use are the most common occurrences. This shows how important healthcare professionals are in increasing caution when administering medication and writing prescriptions. Active pharmacist involvement, system support, and ongoing education can reduce errors and improve patient safety. Keywords : DOAC, Medication Errors, Drug-Related Problems.

title: Exercise blood-pressure responses for atrial fibrillation risk stratification: a systematic review
summary: Blood pressure measured during or immediately after exercise exposes an intermittent haemodynamic stress that resting clinic readings do not capture, and abnormal responses may precede sustained hypertension by years. No existing guideline framework relates these responses to atrial fibrillation (AF) risk. This systematic review synthesises the longitudinal evidence linking exercise blood-pressure responses — exaggerated, blunted, and delayed-recovery phenotypes, together with workload-indexed metrics — to incident or recurrent AF, arrhythmic substrates (left atrial enlargement, diastolic dysfunction, adverse ventricular remodelling), and modification by exercise training. We searched PubMed/MEDLINE (three complementary strategies), Europe PMC, and ClinicalTrials.gov on 28 September 2026, supplemented by citation tracking; 17 studies met the eligibility criteria. Risk of bias was assessed with QUIPS, certainty of evidence with GRADE, and the synthesis follows SWiM; no meta-analysis is planned because exposure definitions across studies are not commensurable. Expected outcomes are phenotype-specific effect estimates, an explicit appraisal of whether responses carry risk information beyond the structural substrate, and a research roadmap for standardised thresholds and upstream prevention. This is a retrospective registration: the search and data extraction were completed before this record was submitted.

title: Multiple Accessory Pathways in Children: Electrophysiological Features and Catheter Ablation Outcomes
summary: Background Multiple accessory pathways (MAPs) may complicate electrophysiological assessment and catheter ablation in pediatric patients. We aimed to evaluate the clinical and electrophysiological characteristics, anatomical distribution, and procedural and follow-up outcomes of pediatric patients with MAPs.Materials and methods This retrospective study included pediatric patients with at least two distinct accessory pathways identified during EPS between November 2019 and February 2026.Results Of 1101 patients who underwent catheter ablation, 619 had accessory pathway-related arrhythmias; among these, 31 (5.0%) had MAPs. The mean age and body weight at the first procedure were 12.1 ± 3.6 years and 44.2 ± 18.8 kg, respectively, and 16 patients were female. Nine patients had structural heart disease, including seven with Ebstein anomaly. A total of 66 accessory pathways were identified: 28 patients had two pathways, two had three, and one had four. The right posteroseptal region was the most common pathway location (27.3%). One patient also had atrioventricular nodal reentrant tachycardia. Complete elimination of all accessory pathways was achieved in 29 of 31 patients (93.5%), and 63 of 66 pathways (95.5%) were successfully ablated. Recurrence occurred in six patients (19.4%). No procedure-related complications were observed during a mean follow-up of 26.3 ± 18.7 months.Conclusion MAPs were successfully treated with high acute success rates and no procedure-related complications. Nevertheless, recurrence and the identification of additional accessory pathways during subsequent evaluations remained clinically relevant, supporting the need for systematic post-ablation reassessment and long-term follow-up.

title: Medication Adherence Patterns for Patients with Atrial Fibrillation: A Mixed Methods Study to Understand Patient and Clinician Perspectives.
summary:
BACKGROUND: Medication adherence is essential for effective atrial fibrillation (AF) management; however, many patients with AF are non-adherent to these medications, necessitating an understanding of adherence barriers. This mixed-methods study aimed to identify factors influencing oral anticoagulant (OAC) adherence.

METHODS: A stratified random sample of 2000 patients with non-valvular AF and OAC prescriptions was surveyed from a large, seven state community health system, capturing barriers and facilitators to medication adherence using an adapted version of the Adherence Starts with Knowledge-12 scale. Twenty-eight semi-structured interviews were conducted with a sample of survey respondents to further explore drivers of adherence. Eligible clinicians were surveyed on patient adherence. Survey data were analyzed descriptively and using multivariable regression models. Interview data were analyzed thematically.

RESULTS: Of 213 patients with an adherence score available, 31.5% reported non-adherence. Nonadherent patients were more likely to report poor healthcare experiences. Receiving all necessary information from clinicians was positively associated with medication adherence. Interview analyses showed clinician communication about medications and believing that medication can help manage AF were important facilitators of medication adherence. While clinician response rate was low (3.0%), 87% of responding clinicians perceived high non-adherence among patients with AF, citing forgetfulness, cost, and side effects as the main reasons.

CONCLUSION: Most patients reported adherence to their medications, whereas clinicians perceived relatively low adherence among their patients. However, clinicians aligned with patients on the need for improved communication and shared decision making around AF treatment. Interventions that promote clinician and patient communication may be pivotal for optimizing medication adherence, which may lead to improved patient care.

title: Left atrial appendage isolation and thrombotic and thromboembolic outcomes in atrial fibrillation: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
summary:
BACKGROUND: Electrical left atrial appendage isolation (LAAI) may be accompanied by impaired appendage function and thromboembolic complications. We evaluated the association between LAAI and clinical stroke or transient ischemic attack (TIA), while separately examining imaging-detected left atrial appendage (LAA) thrombus and related supportive outcomes.

METHODS: PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials were searched from inception to December 6, 2024 for comparative clinical studies reporting thrombotic or thromboembolic outcomes after LAAI. Clinical stroke or TIA was the primary outcome. Risk ratios (RRs) were pooled using an inverse-variance random-effects model with restricted maximum-likelihood estimation and Hartung-Knapp-adjusted confidence intervals (CIs). The preferred primary analysis excluded the smaller Rillig cohort because of possible participant overlap with the Heeger cohort. Imaging-detected LAA thrombus, anticoagulation-at-event data, and LAA functional findings were evaluated separately.

RESULTS: Five comparative observational studies were included. The preferred primary analysis comprised four studies and 3876 patients, including 801 who underwent LAAI and 3075 controls. Clinical stroke or TIA occurred in 42 and 66 patients, respectively. LAAI was associated with a higher cumulative risk of clinical stroke or TIA (RR = 4.96, 95% CI 1.10-22.42; P = 0.043; I2 = 55.6%). The 95% prediction interval was 0.21-115.69. Inclusion of the potentially overlapping Rillig cohort yielded an RR of 5.26 (95% CI 1.80-15.36; P = 0.013), but the prediction interval remained compatible with no association. Leave-one-out analyses were directionally consistent, although statistical significance was lost after omission of Kim, Heeger, or Romero. Comparative LAA thrombus estimates were available only from Rillig (RR = 22.31, 95% CI 1.34-370.43) and Heeger (RR = 10.31, 95% CI 2.50-42.56) and were not pooled because potential cohort overlap could not be excluded. Anticoagulation-at-event and LAA functional data were unsuitable for quantitative synthesis.

CONCLUSIONS: The available evidence suggests that LAAI may be associated with a higher cumulative risk of clinical stroke or TIA. However, the extremely wide prediction interval crossing the null and the loss of statistical significance after omission of several individual studies indicate considerable uncertainty regarding the magnitude and consistency of this potential association across different practice settings. Comparative imaging findings also suggested a higher frequency of postprocedural LAA thrombus, although the available evidence was limited and potentially overlapping. Independent comparative studies with standardized TEE surveillance, clearly defined anticoagulation exposure, and complete clinical and imaging outcome reporting are required.

title: Spatiotemporal Organization of Atrial Fibrillation via EGM and ECG: A Meta-Analysis
summary: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is the most prevalent persistent arrhythmia in clinical practice, and guidance for catheter ablation is still problematic because important targets within the arrhythmogenic substrate are difficult to pinpoint. This study uses both intracardiac electrograms (EGM) and surface electrocardiograms (ECG) to suggest that recurrence percentage (Rec%) can be used as a quantitative biomarker to describe atrial electrical structure. The methodology employed digital signal processing techniques, such as adaptive bandpass filtering and ventricular interference removal, using the Pan-Tompkins and Adaptive Singular Value Cancellation (ASVC) algorithms. The pipeline was validated using a subset of the publicly accessible Intracardiac Atrial Fibrillation Database (n = 3 patients, yielding 12 synchronized spatial mapping points across four anatomical positions: AFW, IVC, SVC, and TVA). Intracardiac Rec% and surface sample entropy (SampEn) were cross-correlated. The results demonstrated a statistically significant inverse correlation (Pearson r = −0.38, p < 0.001) between increasing EGM recurrence percentage and decreasing ECG complexity (SampEn) across the aggregated patient cohort. These results imply that non-invasive surface monitoring can support ablation guidance and rotor identification, providing an alternative to relying solely on invasive recordings and reflecting changes in the intracardiac substrate.

title: Evaluation of a Hybrid RR–P-Wave Approach for Automatic Atrial Fibrillation Detection in ECG Signals
summary: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is a common cardiac arrhythmia associated with an increased risk of stroke and heart failure.This study compares two ECG-based approaches for automatic AF detection using 86 records from PhysioNet databases. The first method (Algorithm 23) is based on RR interval variability and heart rate variability features, whereas the second method (Algorithm 24) extends the baseline model by incorporating Pwave morphological analysis and a detector of abrupt RR transitions. Descriptive analyses showed higher overall performance metrics for the RR-based approach, although paired statistical analyses did not indicate a significant difference between the algorithms at the 5% significance level. A class-specific AFIBanalysis showed that the hybrid model increased sensitivity from 80.0% to 83.3%, but also increased false positives and reduced precision from 77.4% to 64.1%. These findings suggest that P-wave and RR-transition features provide complementary physiological information but require more robust integration strategies based on signal quality assessment, ectopy control, and evidence fusion.

title: Proposal of an Automated System for the Langendorff Isolated Heart Perfusion Method
summary: The Langendorff method of isolated heart perfusion is a well-established ex vivo surgical technique in cardiovascular biological and pharmacological research. However, the accuracy of clinical trials is often limited by the oscillations and variability inherent in the manual control of homeostatic parameters. This research presents the development and benchtop validation of an automation platform applied to the Langendorff method., designed to ensure the rigorous stability of critical variables during cardiac arrhythmia trials, such as atrial fibrillation. The proposed modular architecture is based on the transposition of industrial automation technologies to the laboratory environment, using a Programmable Logic Controller (PLC WEG TPW03) vertically integrated with Elipse E3 SCADA data acquisition and supervision software. The PLC operates deterministically and with low latency to control temperature and actuate peristaltic pumps and solenoid valves, managed via Ladder logic. Preliminary fluid dynamic and thermal validation tests demonstrated that the system, using on-off thermal control on the test bench, stabilized the fluid temperature at a median of 37°C (IQR = 0.10°C; σ-sigma = 0.0699°C), exhibiting statistical superiority over the manual method (p = 4.15 x 10⁻⁷). Thermal control via a PID loop embedded in the PLC is proposed for future implementation directly on the aortic cannula. Coronary flow was precisely regulated and maintained within the physiological range with a median of 23.5 mL/min (IQR = 0.52 mL/min; σ-sigma = 0.39 mL/min), validating the alignment of the control with the predictive allometric model for leporine specimens. Benchtop results confirm that the platform's robustness and determinism eliminate human operational errors and ensure methodological reproducibility, validating the physical-operational control infrastructure as an indispensable preparatory step for future applications in actual biological assays.

title: Fibrosis burden and spatial pattern affect left atrial appendage stasis in multi-beat multi-physics simulations
summary: Abstract Purpose Atrial fibrosis is associated with thromboembolic risk in atrial fibrillation, but it remains unclear how fibrosis-related contractile impairment alters blood transport in the left atrium (LA) and left atrial appendage (LAA). Prior multi-physics simulations coupling electromechanical (EM) and computational fluid dynamics (CFD) models showed that fibrosis impairs LA function and flow, but were limited to booster-only contraction and could not separate the effects of fibrosis burden from its spatial distribution. Here, we examined how fibrosis burden and spatial pattern independently relate to long-term LA and LAA hemodynamics in full-cycle, multi-beat simulations on a common LA anatomy. Methods Three fibrosis patterns derived from late gadolinium enhancement MRI were applied globally to a common LA anatomy at matched burdens of 15.6% and 31.2%, yielding six global-fibrosis cases and a non-fibrotic reference. Two patterns were also confined to the LAA at local burdens of 10%, 25%, and 50%, yielding six LAA-fibrosis cases. A 3D EM model of the LA anatomy coupled to a 0D circulatory model resolved the reservoir, conduit, and booster phases, and the EM-derived wall motion drove subsequent multi-beat CFD simulations. Region-specific emptying fraction (EF), non-dimensional kinetic energy (KE), and the 90th percentile of blood residence time (T R ) were evaluated in the LA and LAA. Results Left ventricular stroke volume remained nearly constant across cases, whereas increasing global fibrosis burden progressively reduced LA and LAA EF (LA: 36% to 30–31%; LAA: 44% to 28–38%), lowered both active and passive LA EF, and monotonically increased LA T R across all patterns. Non-dimensional LA KE showed an approximately quadratic association with LA EF across patterns, whereas LAA KE was more scattered but still increased with LAA EF. In contrast, the 90th percentile of LAA T R did not increase monotonically with decreasing LAA EF for one pattern. When fibrosis was confined to the LAA, non-dimensional LAA KE collapsed onto a single relationship with LAA EF for both patterns, whereas LAA T R followed distinct, non-monotonic trends. Conclusions Fibrosis burden, through its association with functional impairment, predominantly governed whole-LA hemodynamics, whereas LAA stasis additionally depended on the spatial distribution of fibrosis. In the LAA-fibrosis cases, LAA EF was a robust descriptor of chamber-averaged KE regardless of fibrosis pattern, but did not fully explain LAA residence time. These findings support evaluating imaging-derived fibrosis pattern, in addition to fibrosis burden and functional metrics, as a potential determinant of LAA transport and stasis. Its incremental value for thrombogenic-risk assessment requires prospective clinical validation.

title: Cardiac segmentation for ventricular tachycardia radioablation and radiotherapy patients with cardiac implants
summary: Deep-learning (DL) segmentation enables cardiac substructure (CS) delineation for advanced cardiac-sparing radiation therapy (RT). Patients presenting for RT may have implantable devices (cardioverter-defibrillators (ICDs)) and metal artifacts. Stereotactic body RT (SBRT) is used to treat ventricular tachycardia (VT), a population frequently with ICDs. We apply a DL model for RT patients with ICDs or undergoing VT-SBRT, enabling segmentation and CS-level dose analysis. CT simulation (CT-SIM) of 19 patients with ICDs and received VT-SBRT were evaluated. A validated segmentation model was retrained using a highly-curated CT-SIM cohort, supplemented with ICD images for training and validation, with a hold-out ICD test set (n=10), to predict 20 CS. Additional CT-SIM datasets included cancer-RT patients with (n=9) and without (n=10) ICDs to evaluate generalizability. The retrained ICD-supplemented model was compared against a non-ICD model using Dice similarity coefficient (DSC), 95% Hausdorff distance (HD95), and Wilcoxon signed-rank test (p<0.05). Dosimetric evaluation was performed for VT-SBRT CS. For VT-SBRT, the ICD-supplemented model achieved average DSC/HD95 of 0.71(0.19)/10.7(22.5)mm respectively, outperforming (p<0.05) the non-ICD model. On CT-SIM with ICDs, average DSC/HD95 were 0.70(0.22)/7.9(5.1)mm respectively, outperforming (p<0.05) the non-ICD model. On CT-SIM without ICDs, the average DSC was 0.74(0.17) (Non-ICD, DSC, 0.75(0.16), p<0.05) and average HD95 was 5.5(3.1)mm (Non-ICD, HD95, 5.3(2.8mm)). For VT-SBRT, CS dose depended on target location, with higher relative dose delivered to the ventricles, tricuspid valve, atrioventricular node, and left coronary arteries than other CS. ICD-supplemented training improved CS segmentation despite metal artifacts without meaningfully degrading non-ICD performance, supporting segmentation and CS-level dosimetry in ICD populations.

title: Trends in pediatric sudden cardiac death-related mortality in the United States from 1999 to 2020: a nationwide CDC WONDER analysis
summary: Introduction Sudden cardiac death (SCD) in children is rare but devastating, often affecting previously healthy children. Unlike adults, pediatric SCD results from a wide spectrum of uncommon and heterogeneous conditions. Despite recent advancements in understanding and prevention strategies, national data on long-term mortality trends remain limited. Material and methods We analyzed death certificate data from the CDC WONDER database from 1999 to 2020 for SCD-related mortality in individuals aged 0 to 14 years. Age-adjusted mortality rates (AAMRs) per 100,000, with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) and annual percentage changes (APCs) with 95% CIs, were calculated, stratified by year, sex, race, state, urbanization, and census region. Results From 1999 until 2020, 30,675 pediatric SCD-related deaths occurred. The AAMR declined from 2.8 per 100,000 population in 1999 to 2.5 (APC = –6.0%, 95% CI: –10.8 to –0.9) in 2001 and further to 2.0 in 2020 (APC = –1.0%, 95% CI: –1.2 to –0.8). AAMRs were consistently higher in males than in females (1999: 3.2 vs. 2.4; 2020: 2.1 vs. 2.0). When stratified by race, non-Hispanic (NH) Black children had the highest AAMRs. Rates declined in all U.S. regions, with the highest rates observed in the Northeast (3.5 to 1.9) and the lowest in the Midwest (1.7 to 1.2). State-level rate disparities were marked, ranging from 4.9 in Mississippi to as low as 1.1 in Maine, Maryland, and Wisconsin. Conclusions Despite overall declines in SCD-related mortality, significant disparities persist across sex, race, region, and urbanization.

title: Complete Heart Block in Young Patient With Systemic Lupus Erythematosus: A Case Report
summary: Complete heart block is a rare but serious cardiac complication of systemic lupus erythematosus.Most reported cases present with symptoms such as syncope.In this report, we describe the case of a 33-year-old woman with systemic lupus erythematosus who was diagnosed with asymptomatic Complete heart block.This case highlights the importance of proactive cardiac evaluation, including a baseline electrocardiogram, in systemic lupus erythematosus patients to detect clinically silent conduction defects that may carry a risk of sudden cardiac death.

title: Increased Premature Ventricular Contraction Burden During Exercise Stress Testing with Surgical Face Masks: A Retrospective Cohort Study
summary: Introduction: The physiological impact of surgical face masks on exercise-induced arrhythmias remains poorly understood. This study aimed to evaluate changes in premature ventricular contraction (PVC) burden during exercise stress testing performed with and without surgical masks.Methods: We retrospectively analyzed 41 patients who underwent exercise ECG stress testing with and without face mask. Inclusion criteria included age 18–75 years, treadmill exercise with ≥85% maximum predicted heart rate, and absence of ischemia or significant arrhythmias. PVC burden was calculated as the ratio of PVC beats to total beats during exercise. Paired t-tests compared PVC burden with and without masks.Results: PVC burden was significantly higher during masked testing (0.91% ± 0.38) compared to unmasked testing (0.52% ± 0.25) (p < 0.001). Seventy-one percent of patients demonstrated increased PVC burden with masks, and 44% exhibited increases greater than 0.3%, potentially clinically relevant. No sustained arrhythmias or test terminations occurred.Discussion and conclusion: Surgical face mask use during exercise stress testing is associated with increased PVC burden, likely due to mild hypoxia or autonomic stress. Awareness of this effect is important for interpretation of exercise-induced arrhythmias during masked testing. Further prospective studies incorporating oxygen saturation and autonomic monitoring are warranted.

title: Challenges in pregnancy of a patient with cardiac sarcoidosis on implantable cardioverter defibrillator: a case report
summary: Cardiac sarcoidosis (CS) can present as ventricular tachycardia (VT) and cardiac arrest. Management of VT in CS is difficult and includes disease-specific agents, such as steroids, antiarrhythmic drugs (AADs), and implantation of an implantable cardioverter-defibrillator (ICD). With the advent of ICD technology in recent decades, patients with inherited or congenital cardiomyopathy have a greater chance of survival into adulthood. Women with ICDs in this group are now more likely to reach reproductive age. We report a case of a 24-year-old Primi, known case of CS with recurrent VT managed with ICD, immunosuppressants and steroids. Five months later, the patient became pregnant. A multidisciplinary approach was sought throughout her pregnancy with contribution from a cardiologist and rheumatologist. Along with cardiologist team and anaesthetist team our patient delivered an alive female baby at 36 weeks. Regular follow-up and timely delivery made this high-risk pregnancy successful.

title: Delayed cardiac conduction disease in a young adult following childhood Chagas infection
summary: Presentation A Bolivian man in his 30s presented to the ED with non-exertional chest pain and intermittent second-degree atrioventricular (2:1) block.Diagnosis Given a history of untreated childhood Trypanosoma cruzi infection and family history of Chagas heart disease, late cardiac manifestation was suspected. Structural and ischaemic causes were excluded.Treatment Antiparasitic therapy was initiated. Pacemaker implantation was considered but deferred following shared decision-making due to absence of symptoms.Discussion Chagas heart disease (CHD) may present decades after infection with conduction abnormalities. Recognition in the ED is essential to enable appropriate management and reduce the risk of progression to complete heart block and sudden cardiac death.

title: Four Distinct Morphologies of Bundle Branch Reentrant Ventricular Tachycardia Eliminated by Right Bundle Branch Ablation

Development of a prospective clinical workflow for proton beam therapy of ventricular tachycardia.
summary:
PURPOSE: This study presents a prospective preclinical workflow for proton beam therapy of refractory ventricular tachycardia (VT), covering target transfer, treatment planning (TP), and beam gating.

METHODS: Photon-based stereotactic arrhythmia radioablation (STAR) protocols were adapted to proton beam therapy, encompassing (i) target transfer from electroanatomical mapping (EAM) onto planning computed tomography (CT), (ii) simulation of three TP cases from the Standardized Treatment and Outcome Platform for Stereotactic Therapy of Re-Entrant Tachycardia by a Multidisciplinary (STOPSTORM.eu) benchmark, and (iii) evaluation of trigger events and delays for synchrotron beam delivery control using gating.

RESULTS: CARDIO-RT enabled electroanatomical mapping to computed tomography (EAM-to-CT) target transfer; two experienced cardiologists qualitatively judged the transferred targets as clinically acceptable by visual inspection. Treatment plans demonstrated effective organ at risk (OAR) sparing and clinical adequacy. The planning target volume (PTV) D95% ranged from 23.3 to 23.9 Gy relative biological effectiveness (RBE) and the clinical target volume electrophysiology (CTV [EP]) D95% from 30.9 to 31.6 Gy (RBE); underdosage was permitted where anatomical compromise was unavoidable. No CTV(EP) hotspot exceeded 33.5 Gy (RBE). Optical trigger signals are supported for beam gating; the total cardiac gating chain latency was below 30 ms.

CONCLUSION: This technical feasibility study demonstrates a prospective preclinical workflow for proton beam STAR, covering EAM-to-CT target transfer, TP across three benchmark clinical cases, and accelerator-side optical gating integration at a synchrotron-based facility. The workflow demonstrates technical feasibility; however, full clinical translation still requires patient positioning and verification, motion characterization, and end-to-end validation. Future work will employ a dynamic anthropomorphic phantom to characterize motion-induced dosimetric changes and assess plan robustness for proton and carbon ion beam delivery.

title: Association Between Earthquake Exposure and Tachyarrhythmias: A Systematic Review
summary: Background: Major earthquakes impose sudden physical and psychological stress and may trigger cardiac rhythm disturbances, yet evidence on post-earthquake tachyarrhythmias remains inconsistent. We reviewed comparative studies reporting tachyarrhythmia-related outcomes after earthquake exposure. Methods: We searched PubMed, Europe PMC, ScienceDirect, OpenAlex, and Google Scholar through 31 August 2026 for comparative observational studies published from January 2016 onward. Eligible outcomes were tachyarrhythmias or arrhythmia-directed therapies as defined by each study. Risk of bias was assessed using ROBINS-E domains. Because study designs, outcomes, observation periods, and statistical structures differed substantially, we did not pool results; reporting was informed by SWiM principles. Results: Five studies met eligibility criteria from 19 verified de-duplicated records. Ranjbar et al. reported increased sustained ventricular arrhythmia, whereas SVT did not increase significantly. Chan et al. found no increase in ventricular arrhythmias or device therapy after two Christchurch earthquakes. Babić et al. observed more paroxysmal arrhythmias requiring electrical cardioversion near the epicentres. Yıldırım et al. reported more AF admissions but no significant increase in VT. Polat et al. found increased device-detected ventricular arrhythmia and therapy, particularly subacutely. Three independent risk-ratio estimates from two studies were displayed without pooling; all five studies contributed to direction-of-effect synthesis. Conclusions: Earthquake exposure may be associated with more tachyarrhythmic events in selected settings, but findings vary by population, outcome, and post-earthquake period. The evidence remains limited and heterogeneous. Better designed prospective multicentre studies are needed.

title: Integrating High-Resolution Electrophysiological Mapping with Histological Remodeling in a Rabbit Model of Ventricular Tachycardia
summary: Cardiac arrhythmias are the result of complex interplay between the heart's electrical activity and structural architecture. Ventricular Tachycardia (VT), a leading cause of sudden cardiac mortality, necessitates substrate mapping and signal analysis to identify arrhythmogenic channels and scars for targeted ablation. However, the link between local electrical and optical signals—acquired concurrently through optical and electrical mapping—and the underlying tissue architecture has rarely been objectively documented. This study sought to assess the spatial relationship between electrophysiological mapping and myocardial microstructure undergoing VT. Perfused with the Langendorff system, two New Zealand Rabbits hearts underwent VT induction using 1 µM carbachol and an S1-S2 procedure (100 bursts, 2 ms pulses, 1.3 s intervals), and one served as a control. High-resolution electrical and optical mapping were used. Myocardial tissue corresponding to each electrode (n=36 tissue samples) location was carefully collected and processed for histological examination. Our results revealed that structural remodeling was spatially different across electrode-mapped regions. Certain regions had tissue organization comparable to the control heart, whereas others had, myocyte disarray, increased intercellular space, and mild to moderate interstitial cell infiltration. Moreover, areas with nearly normal histological appearance showed abnormal signals. The findings reveal a complex and non-uniform link between myocardial structure and electrical activity. Cellular disorganization contributes to arrhythmia formation but does not always result in abnormal electrical activity underneath the electrode. Voltage mapping was consistent with these observations. Depending solely on voltage mapping may overlook key structural substrates. This study underlines the relevance of integrating electrophysiological mapping with spatially comprehensive histology in experimental research. Such approach may increase our understanding of the disease mechanism, identify arrhythmogenic substrates and improve the precision of ablation methods.

title: Risk Classification for Sudden Cardiac Death Using Single-Lead ECG
summary: Cardiovascular diseases (CVDs) remain the leading cause of death worldwide in both developed and developing countries. A significant portion of these deaths is associated with sudden cardiac death (SCD), an unexpected event frequently triggered by cardiac arrhythmias that compromise the heart's ability to pump blood effectively. The electrocardiogram (ECG) is the most widely used non-invasive tool to evaluate the functional status of the heart, as it records the electrical activity generated by the depolarization and repolarization of the cardiac chambers. The objective of this work is to propose and evaluate a parameter-optimized 1D-CNN, seeking to enable classification with reduced patient-dependency bias. To measure its true efficiency and generalization capacity, the model is contrasted with established approaches in literature. Data from 19 patients from the same database were used, with 15 assigned for training and 4 for validation. The data were digitally processed using a digital filter, subsequently segmented into 5-second intervals, and normalized. Intervals considered normal and high-risk were separated based on database annotations. The data was used to train a one-dimensional convolutional neural network with four convolutional layers, a Global Average Pooling (GAP) layer, a dense layer, and an output layer. The results yielded an overall accuracy of 96.69%, sensitivity for high-risk findings of 94.31%, sensitivity for normal findings of 97.91%, specificity of 97.39%, and an Area Under the Curve (AUC) of 0.9894. The results demonstrate the system's applicability for sudden death risk detection, serving as a potential auxiliary tool in clinical diagnosis.

title: A Short-Scale Transition into Ventricular Fibrillation: Recurrence Quantification and the Limits of Minute-Scale Anticipation
summary: Sudden cardiac death from ventricular fibrillation requires intervention within minutes, motivating tools that detect signal deterioration before the collapse. This work applies Recurrence Quantification Analysis to recordings from the Sudden Cardiac Death Holter Database, extracting fifteen topological metrics over five-second windows under an adaptive recurrence threshold defined as a percentile of the positive pairwise distances of each window. Recurrence matrices and per-window metrics were stored in a traceable manner, and the temporal evolution of the attributes was assessed by visual inspection of the normalized trajectories and distributions. The recurrence descriptors characterize the transition sharply at its onset, where the organized structure of the heartbeat breaks down and the determinism and laminarity metrics undergo an abrupt inflection; a conservative per-patient baseline-departure test found no recording departing from its own baseline band before that instant. However, a per-patient test found no generalized metric separating the baseline window (−60 to −30 min) from the near-collapse window (−30 to 0 min) in the amplitude domain (paired Cohen's d, dz = −0.141, 95% CI [−0.594, 0.348]). The same pipeline applied over a Takens-embedded heart-rate variability series raised the separation to dz = 0.570 (95% CI [−0.617, 1.552]); however, a control restricting the amplitude arm to the same seven patients yielded a comparable dz = 0.517, showing the contrast was confounded by sample reduction. The main contribution is a documented negative result for minute-scale anticipation in both domains, together with a controlled demonstration that an apparent amplitude-versus-variability contrast is explained by sample reduction rather than by domain.
